scope.summary: Bound the parser work that nested malformed '[' input drives in sqlparser: classify_raw and the public semantic_read_plan_checked share an 8-square-bracket pre-parser budget and refuse beyond it with typed fail-closed results (Forbidden / reason_category Other / 'parser square-bracket budget', and PlanMismatch::ParserWorkBudgetExceeded). The classify_fuzz timeout reproducer is committed to the fuzz corpus and pinned by regression tests.
out_of_scope: Other super-linear sqlparser shapes not reached by a 300 s campaign (the campaign is bounded evidence, not a proof of absence).
Admitting bracket-heavy literal text: 9+ '[' anywhere in a statement (including inside string literals) is now refused; this is tighten-only by design.

entry_points.name: production reachability
entry_points.trace: semantic_read_plan_checked is the public planner reached from the read executor and the oracle_explain_plan hard-parse path (per the implementer audit); the budget is enforced inside that function, so every caller is bounded regardless of whether classify ran first.

limitations: Pre-fix timing measured in a release build without sanitizers (2.6 s); the CI libFuzzer timeout (>10 s) was under ASan/coverage instrumentation.
The bead title attributes the stall to classify(); measurement shows classify was already fast and fail-closed pre-fix, and the stall was the semantic planner. The fix covers both entry points.

The budget counts '[' bytes anywhere, including string literals and comments, so a query with 9 or more '[' in literal data is now refused (typed). This is tighten-only and was accepted by the bead, but it can over-refuse bracket-heavy literal text.
